Why: Radical halogenation of alkanes: intermediate = alkyl radical ($\text{R}\cdot$, planar $sp^2$ carbon), regio = favors more substituted C–H ($3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$); $\text{Br}_2$ is much more selective ($1:82:1640$) than $\text{Cl}_2$ ($1:3.8:5$), stereo = racemization at the radical carbon (planar achiral radical intermediate attacked from both faces)

Why: Gilman (Diorganocopper / Corey–House) coupling: intermediate = triorganocopper(III) intermediate (undergoes reductive elimination to R–R'), regio = C–C bond forms strictly at the original C–Cu and C–X positions (no rearrangement!), stereo = **retention of stereochemistry** at vinylic double bonds; inversion at 1°/2° alkyl halides
